differences.what: The label construction itself: the bilinear forms (<t_S,t_T>=|S cap T|-1 over Q, the dot product over F_2) make every triple line nondegenerate and neighbouring triple lines orthogonal, in an m-dimensional F^{(x)3}. A only says 'nested nondegenerate subspaces of an m-dimensional space'.
The side-edge inclusion: t_X perp t_Y gives <t_X> subset t_Y^perp. This is L2 in part: the complement <t_X,t_Y>^perp of dimension h-2 is not stated.
Identifies what the decreasing centre edge 3->4 loses (the summand P(x)F, dimension h). A gives only the dimension h.

items.note: Both plans carry L3 (telescoping to Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich) and L5 (100/539, 101/539), and neither has the residual table (L1) or the orthonormal-basis argument (L4). B adds the bilinear-form construction that makes the labels nest, and part of L2; A has nothing on this item that B lacks.

differences.what: Weight is additive mod 4 for orthogonal binary vectors, so q_V-q_U=sum_v wt(v)[v.x] over an orthonormal residual basis.
wt(v) is odd, so the phase is i^{eps[v.x]}; conjugating by H turns it into the translation kernel aI+bX_v or its inverse.

A only names 'source and sink corrections'. B also omits that the zero/full labels give frames I and C^{(x)m} and that X outputs are negated.
The kernel count s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c<W_c m, with no extra source term and deficit 2N-2L_c. A never states s_c's value or that it is below W_c m.

differences.what: The conjugation C_{U+}C_{U-}^{-1}=P_M(prod_j C_{e_j}^{eps_j})P_M^{-1}, with M an invertible binary matrix whose first columns are the residual basis. This puts each directional kernel on one coordinate slot, so it is one child call. A only states the product of directional kernels C_{v_j} and never moves them to slots.
Gaussian elimination writes M as at most m(m-1)+3m elementary row additions, each an XOR of selected bits across two whole slots. This reduces the non-recursive work to binary row additions.

differences.what: The tape cost: at most sixteen chunk swaps (O(VL^tau) each, by the arbitrary-width interchange) and eight O(V) rotations.
The full time bound O(V(L^tau+1)+MA^3+delta_bad MA(R+A)), and the family conditions that make the extra terms o(1). A says only 'plus negligible terms'.
The omitted last selected position is done by a separate two-bit XOR.

The computed chirp transform: phase numerators mod 2r, then x_0=Q_p(conj(a~) x), y_0=M_C(a~,x_0), C~(x)=Q_p(conj(a~) y_0), with exact counterpart Q F_t x. A only summarizes it as 'a chirp transform evaluated by a twisted ring convolution'.
Why S appears twice: the first scale gives w=(u*v)/S and the second, with 2^{2b+4}, gives the integer convolution. A explains only the first.

Neither plan states the liminf form of the negation of an eventual n lg n lower bound (lines 379-387). Both only rely on an 'n-log-n-conjecture' concept at S0.

chain.note: Both trees follow the paper's route: digit convolution, CRT, Gaussian resampling with chirp, twisted ring convolution with synthetic transforms, two fast tape procedures, exact recovery, cost table. A carries the central saving only for the bit network: s_b<W_b m, then s/W<m^tau, then F_k=O(e^tau), then O(Vu^tau). For the butterfly layer A never derives s_c<W_c m or s_c/W_c<m^sigma, its S3.3.e uses a=s/W<=m^sigma without support, and it lacks the P_M step that turns residual kernels into slot-wise children. B's S5 derives both savings (s_b and s_c with eta_b and eta_c, giving tau=sigma), then both recurrences, with the P_M conjugation linking the complex network to the layer recursion.

overall.reason: Neither plan misstates the paper. The decisive difference is the complex half of the central saving. B gives s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c<W_c m with eta_b and eta_c (so s_c/W_c<m^sigma), the phase-interface mechanism (weight additivity mod 4, odd weight giving the translation kernel aI+bX_v, the 27-coordinate C^{-1} correction), and the P_M conjugation that makes each residual vector one slot-wise child. A lacks all of these, so its butterfly-layer recursion rests on an unproved s/W<=m^sigma. The remaining differences are smaller and mostly favour B (the label bilinear forms and the L2 inclusion, the guard-width constants C_0 and C_1); A's few extras (base case, exponent list, output length) are minor.
